description_full: Ubiquiti Inc. engages in the development of networking technology for service providers, enterprises, and consumers in North America, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, Asia Pacific, South America. The company develops technology platforms for high-capacity distributed Internet access and unified information technology. Its service provider product platforms offer carrier-class network infrastructure for fixed wireless broadband, wireless backhaul systems, and routing and related software; and enterprise product platforms provide wireless LAN infrastructure, video surveillance products, switching and routing solutions, security gateways, door access systems, and other WLAN products. It also provides technology platforms, such as UniFi Cloud Gateway, an Enterprise class internet and security gateway device; UniFi Wi-Fi, an enterprise Wi-Fi system; UniFi Protect, a video surveillance platform; UniFi Switch that deliver performance, switching, and power of ethernet support for enterprise networks; UniFi Access, a door access solution; UniFi Talk, a plug-and-play phone system and VoIP subscription service. In addition, the company offers airMAX, which include proprietary protocols that contain technologies for minimizing signal noise; airFiber, a wireless backhauls point-to-point radio system; UFiber GPON, a plug and play fiber network technology to build high speed fiber internet networks; and Wave, a technology platform. Further, the company provides base stations, radios, backhaul equipment, and customer premise equipment; embedded radio products; and antennas. It serves customers through a network of distributors, online retailers, and direct to customers through webstores. The company was formerly known as Ubiquiti Networks, Inc. and changed its name to Ubiquiti Inc. in August 2019. Ubiquiti Inc. was incorporated in 2003 and is headquartered in New York, New York.

financial_summary: Ubiquiti Inc. is a large-cap technology business with a $35.9B market cap on $3.3B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +19% over the past three years and +17% annually across the full decade, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.
Returns on capital run at 102% against a 10% cost of capital — a 92-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat, with gross margins sitting at 44%.

The business throws off $909M in free cash flow — roughly 28 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, with adequate 0.97× cash conversion.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year.

Shareholder yield is only 0.5%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 93% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and within its sector the business captures 1.5× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.

The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.03 across 530 companies in the universe; the top four hold 29% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares have drifted lower, down 17% over the past year excluding the latest month.
The price sits near the bottom of its 52-week range, 46% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 53% and a beta of 1.10, it moves roughly with the market.
About $65.4M trades a day, enough to build a position.

val: The price sits above its DCF fair value of $427 (margin of safety -39%), so there is no valuation cushion.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 27%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $296 to $631 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
On multiples it looks expensive against Technology peers: P/E 37.4 vs 26.7, EV/EBITDA 25.4 vs 16.4 and P/FCF 39.5 vs 25.4 (sector median).
Against its own history it is dear: the EBIT multiple sits 3% above its 10-year median.
Earnings yields are thin: an FCF yield of 2.5% (below the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 3.9% (vs the 8% bar).
The 2 covering analysts target $734 on average, 24% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
prof: ROIC of 102% clears the cost of capital of 10.2% by 92pp, the mark of a value creator; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.46).
It runs a 44% gross margin and converts 28% of revenue into free cash flow.
ROE of 67% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (1.5x equity multiplier).
It spends 6.2% of revenue on R&D and 0.2% on stock compensation.
hlth: The balance sheet carries net cash of $531.2M.
No distress or manipulation flags (Altman Z 33.2, in the safe zone).
Its debt comes due soon (maturity wall about 0.5 years out), so refinancing terms matter.
The Beneish M-score (-2.09) sits just under the manipulation line, so earnings quality bears watching.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 19.0% over 3 years, 11.5% over 5 years and 17.3% over 10 years, so growth is accelerating, and it has been lumpy (year-to-year swings of 87%).
At current returns, reinvesting 78% of profits supports about 30.0% a year of fundamental growth, enough to sustain growth.
Free cash flow has compounded 8.9% a year over five years.
Capex roughly matches depreciation (1.0x, 0.6% of sales), a maintenance pace.
Its Rule of 40 score is 39, below the 40 that marks a healthy growth business.
own: Insiders own 93.0%, meaningful skin in the game, and institutions hold 5%.
Shareholder yield is a modest 0.5% (0.7% in dividends).
people: With about 1,818 employees, each generates about $1.8M of revenue, 4.8x the Technology median, and productivity has risen 17.2% a year.
That works out to $500K of free cash flow per employee.
The company is founder-led, which often keeps management aligned with long-term owners.
CEO pay is $1.1M (1x revenue per employee).
